# Button

A control that commits an action on this screen.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:light" title="Button examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-button--docs">Open Button in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Every action.

- **Use it when:** The press does something here: save, submit, delete, open a dialog, go to the next step.
- **Not when:** The press only takes people to another page, or flips a setting that should persist.

Instead:

- [Toggle](./toggle.md): An on or off setting that should persist as state.
- Link: Navigation to another page or section.

## Why it works this way

Button looks the way it does because of 8 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Button, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-outcomes-q1"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>Which outcome matters most?</b><code>outcomes.q1</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Completion without errors</div><p>Finished sign-ups and orders.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>primary</b>: One clear action per view.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>large</b>: One clear action per view, at the normal size, in every brand.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: default</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-color-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many emphasis levels do actions need?</b><code>color.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Three</div><p>Primary, secondary and ghost in every brand.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>secondary</b>: The alternative that steps back, and the first step of a delete.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Moving through the page or a dialog. | Tab lands on the button in a logical order. | The control is skipped because it used HTML disabled. |
| The button is focused and the person confirms. | Enter runs the same action as a click. | Enter only works on submit buttons. |
| The button is focused. | Space runs the same action as a click. | Space scrolls the page instead. |
| The button opened a dialog, menu or popover that just closed. | After the action closes a surface, focus returns to the button. | Focus dropped on the page body. |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The control has a name assistive tech can speak. Any button, especially an icon-only one.
- [ ] The focused control stays visible; color alone is not the cue. Keyboard or assistive-tech focus is on the button.
- [ ] Unavailable stays in the tab order and explains why. The action must not run, but focus must not jump away.
- [ ] A button that stays down exposes its pressed state. Pin, follow, or another sticky on or off on a button.
- [ ] A button that opens something exposes open or closed. The press reveals a menu, panel or more content.
- [ ] The hit area stays usable, including at a small size. Touch, pointer, or a compact toolbar button.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add button
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Button reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.

### Its own variables
